detail: Ordinal sequencing in abstract for multi-model papers
statement: In C-type abstracts with multiple models, use ordinal adverbs (Firstly/Secondly/Thirdly/Finally) to open each model-result paragraph.
procedure: Open each abstract paragraph with ordinal adverb
Each paragraph: model name + method + key metric
positive_pattern: Ordinal adverbs create scannable roadmap through multi-model abstracts

statement: Open model sections with one-sentence textbook definition of the method before applying to the specific problem.
procedure: Follow with specific application to problem
positive_pattern: Concept-first openers establish accessibility before technical depth

statement: When visual diagnostics suggest a property (e.g., non-stationarity), follow immediately with a formal statistical test (e.g., ADF) using 'To ensure/confirm our judgment'.
procedure: Present visual evidence with figure reference
Introduce formal test with 'To ensure our judgment'
positive_pattern: Visual observation → formal test chain demonstrates methodological rigor

statement: Open sensitivity sections with 'In order to explore the effect of [parameter] on [output], we adjusted [parameter] from [baseline] to [variants].'
procedure: State purpose with 'In order to explore'
positive_pattern: Purpose-method sentence immediately frames what is being tested and why

statement: In strengths sections, each bullet should name a specific model and claim a specific capability, not generic praise.
procedure: Start each bullet with model name
Follow with specific capability verb phrase
positive_pattern: Model-specific strengths are verifiable; generic strengths are empty

statement: State weaknesses directly: 'The model does not account for X' or 'The accuracy of Y% is not sufficient.' Avoid defensive framing.
positive_pattern: Direct weakness statements are more credible than hedged admissions

statement: For time series forecasting: (1) visual stationarity check, (2) ADF test, (3) differencing if needed, (4) ACF/PACF for order selection, (5) AIC/BIC for confirmation.
positive_pattern: Complete ARIMA pipeline from raw data to specified model

statement: When ground-truth labels don't exist: (1) cluster on outcome features, (2) validate clusters, (3) train classifier on input features using cluster labels as targets.
procedure: Use cluster IDs as supervised labels
positive_pattern: Two-stage pipeline creates interpretable classes from unlabeled data

statement: When predicting a distribution across multiple bins (e.g., try counts), use Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts to share representations while allowing task-specific specialization.
procedure: Define expert networks for shared features
Add gating networks for soft routing
Task-specific tower layers for each output
positive_pattern: MMoE leverages task relatedness while allowing specialization

statement: Report both AIC and BIC for model selection. Dual criteria provide stronger justification than single criterion.
procedure: Compute AIC and BIC for candidate models
Note if they agree or disagree
positive_pattern: Dual criteria reporting adds credibility to model selection

statement: When classification accuracy is moderate (e.g., 70%), report it directly and acknowledge insufficiency in weaknesses rather than spinning as positive.
procedure: Acknowledge if insufficient in weaknesses section
positive_pattern: Honest reporting of moderate results builds credibility

statement: When visually identifying outliers, use color highlighting (e.g., red dots) on scatter plots with smooth lines to make anomalies immediately visible.
procedure: Create scatter plot with smooth line
positive_pattern: Color-highlighted outliers are self-documenting: reader sees what was removed

statement: When using K-means, present both elbow method plot AND silhouette score to justify cluster count choice.
positive_pattern: Dual validation (elbow + silhouette) is more convincing than either alone

statement: When a time series has distinct variance regimes, truncate to the lower-variance regime rather than modeling heteroscedasticity. Document the trade-off.
positive_pattern: Truncation for stationarity is pragmatic when sample is large enough

statement: Enumerate all simplifying assumptions in a numbered list before modeling begins. Each assumption should be one sentence.
positive_pattern: Explicit assumption enumeration helps reader judge model validity
